mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (more than 1% quarter-over-quarter) indicates a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 drops and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (more than 0.5% in a month) signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (more than 1% month-over-month) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (more than 5% month-over-month) indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (more than 100,000 jobs lost in a month) signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure in a high-rate environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is negative and the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals a recessionary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity contracts.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 0% QoQ and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of negative GDPC1 and rising UNRATE on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
